title: Lilongwe protest over fuel shortage and energy-sector officials
location: Lilongwe, Malawi; street route and Lilongwe Community Centre area
organizer: Centre for Democracy and Economic Initiatives (CDEDI); supported by Public Affairs Committee, UTM and DPP

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Source establishes a public protest with protesters in streets and at the Lilongwe Community Centre, but supplies no attendance count or evidence sufficient to infer at least 50 simultaneous participants.

start_date.summary: Article dated 25 Nov reports police dispersed a protest in Lilongwe on Monday; exact calendar date is explicit.

location.summary: Article dateline and text locate the protest in Lilongwe, including Lilongwe Community Centre.

demands.summary: Protesters demanded the energy minister and MERA chief resign over the fuel shortage.

participants.summary: Article confirms protesters/gathering but gives no count; threshold unknown.

organizer.summary: CDEDI issued the call; PAC and opposition parties supported it.

state_response.summary: Police used tear gas to disperse the protest; article says no casualties or arrests had been reported.

notes: One report only; source says organizer vowed to continue, but later continuation is not established here. Record is not a final inclusion decision.
open_questions: Can a separate contemporary source establish at least 50 simultaneous participants?
Was there a later gathering from the organizer's stated intention to continue, and what date did it occur?
What was the protest's start/end time and route beyond the Community Centre area?

title: Machinga TTC student march over unpaid allowances and college supplies
location: Machinga Teacher Training College to Machinga District Council offices, Machinga
organizer: Not identified; student union general secretary was quoted

threshold_50_evidence.summary: A student march is reported but no attendance count or qualifying size estimate is given; 50 simultaneous participants not established.

start_date.summary: The item is dated Nov 5 and describes students marching that day.

location.summary: Students were marching from Machinga TTC toward Machinga District Council offices.

demands.summary: Reported grievances were unpaid allowances and essential supply shortages; student union representative said allowances should be addressed urgently.

participants.summary: No participant count or crowd-size description appears.

state_target.summary: Article reports march to District Council offices to submit grievances; public administration target is indicated, but precise jurisdiction over the full grievance set remains unverified.

organizer.summary: Student union representative quoted, but formal organizer is not named.

notes: Separate event from Lilongwe Nov 25 fuel protest. Only one secondary report opened; do not infer petition delivery or a wider national campaign.
open_questions: Can a contemporary independent source establish attendance of at least 50 simultaneous participants?
Was a grievance letter actually delivered to the District Commissioner, and who received it?
Were the allowances funded or controlled by state policy?
When did the march end and what response followed?

title: Lilongwe Old Town protest for electoral reforms
organizer: Opposition protesters; specific organizer not identified in the opened account

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Both CIVICUS and contemporaneous Nation Online describe demonstrators/protesters gathered in Lilongwe but neither provides a simultaneous participant count; threshold 50 remains unknown.

start_date.summary: Nation article published Nov 14 says the disrupted march happened the prior day; CIVICUS independently assigns Nov 13.

location.summary: Nation locates gathering at Lilongwe Community Centre ground in Old Town; CIVICUS also says Old Town, Lilongwe.

demands.summary: Both describe electoral-reform/process demands; Nation specifies concerns about MEC, NRB and Smartmatic system.

participants.summary: Both report protesters/gathering but give no count.

state_response.summary: CIVICUS says police had earlier used tear gas and stood by as thugs attacked; Nation reports masked men chased protesters, police had earlier tear-gassed them and stood by. Do not attribute the thugs’ violence to protesters or definitively to the state.

organizer.summary: The report identifies opposition protesters but no organizer.

notes: Retrospective CIVICUS account only; linked Nation article not yet accessed. Thug violence is not coded as participant violence or state violence. Candidate distinct from Nov25 fuel protest. Contemporary Nation report supports the event date and gathering; no attendance estimate. CIVICUS relationship to the Nation story may not be independent because it links to a Nation article.
open_questions: Can any source establish at least 50 simultaneous participants?
What exact electoral changes were demanded and were demands directed to government agencies?
What state action occurred during the attack beyond tear gas before the attack and reported non-intervention?
Did the march begin, and where/how did it end?
Is the retrospective CIVICUS account derived from the Nation article?

title: St Joseph TTC student protest over delayed upkeep allowances
location: St Joseph Teachers Training College and Dedza District Council, Dedza
organizer: Student union; exact organizer not identified; student union vice-president quoted

threshold_50_evidence.summary: MANA says students staged a protest but gives no count. The reported 575 enrolled students and 181 who received allowances are not protest attendance.

start_date.summary: MANA dated Nov 7 reports the event on Wednesday afternoon, Nov 6.

location.summary: Protest was by St Joseph TTC students in Dedza; petition presented to Dedza District Council.

demands.summary: Textual grievance was delayed monthly upkeep allowances plus college supplies/equipment; no codebook demand category assigned pending interpretation of policy target.

participants.summary: No participant turnout count. 575 enrolled and 181 paid figures are not crowd size.

organizer.summary: Student-union vice-president is quoted; formal organizer details not reported.

state_response.summary: District Council director confirmed receiving the petition and promised to engage authorities; no realized remedy documented.

notes: Separate local college action from Nov 5 Machinga march and Lilongwe TTC boycott reported Dec 3; all concern student allowances, but shared coordination/onset episode is unknown. Enrollment counts are not turnout. Tool followed automatic same-host redirect with %3A decoded; local assessment had evaluated the original encoded target only, and no second request was made.
open_questions: Can a source establish how many students attended this protest at once?
Was this coordinated with other teacher-college actions over allowances?
Which state policy or agency controlled the allowances, and how direct was the demand to that state authority?
When did the gathering end and was the promised council action implemented?

title: Possible Ndirande crowd confrontation over fuel scarcity and Minister Kunkuyu's convoy

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Search results use 'crowd' but provide no count; at least 50 simultaneous participants is unproven.

event.summary: Search snippets describe residents confronting officials and Minister Kunkuyu's convoy in Ndirande; the first exact article URL redirected to an unrelated biography and the Times article remains search-only.

location.summary: Search snippets place the incident in Ndirande, Blantyre.

start_date.summary: One snippet says Friday and carries a Nov 23, 2024 publication date, but no body was obtained; date remains unknown.

demands.summary: Snippets associate confrontation with fuel scarcity and officials' visit; exact participant demand remains pending body evidence.

participants.summary: Snippet says 'crowd' but reports no headcount or estimate.

state_response.summary: Search result says police were called to restore order, but not body-verified.

notes: This is a search-only lead, not an established qualifying protest. MW24N014's requested article redirected to an unrelated 2026 biography; do not retry. MW24N017 is a different Times Group URL; another Times page produced a verification challenge, so no body request was attempted pending exact-scope review. Relationship between the reports is unknown.
open_questions: Can a permitted source confirm the actual occurrence, exact date and domestic state demand?
How many people were simultaneously present?
Did the crowd directly demand fuel-policy changes or only confront officials?
What was the state's response, and was anyone injured/arrested?
Can a source outside the affected Times/MWFN target paths independently document the incident?
